card.architecture: MiniMax-H3 ref2va (Qwen3-VL 32B, int8 ConvRot) — REFERENCE-TO-VIDEO with native audio
card.summary: Generate a first/last-frame-constrained clip with additional semantic references and NATIVE stereo audio. The first frame anchors the timeline; media added through the ＋ ref picker condition identity, appearance, motion, or sound. Output is an mp4 with a baked-in audio track.
use_cases: reference→video: place a referenced subject into a new clip with synchronized sound
multi-reference identity (subject from several angles / a few characters)
first/last-frame clips with reference-supported identity or motion
card.pick_when: You want to animate a first frame while using extra image, video, or audio references for identity, style, motion, or voice.

prompt.guidance: Write H3's six-section Context-IR prompt: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, and non_diegetic_music. Define reusable people, objects, scenes, and styles as <Subject N> sourced from exact attachment tags (<Picture N>, <Video N>, <Audio N>), then state explicitly what must be fully preserved.
prompt.example:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>; preserve her facial identity, hair, age, and clothing.

summary:
[reference generation] <Subject 1> walks through a rain-lit city plaza while remaining fully recognizable.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the face, hair, body proportions, and clothing from <Picture 1>.

detailed_description:
The target video is realistic and cinematic. [Shot 1] <Subject 1> walks slowly toward the camera across wet pavement, glances left, and remains centered during a steady dolly-back. Warm storefront light reflects in the rain.

overall_soundscape:
Soft city traffic, footsteps on wet pavement, and distant crowd ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
A restrained, moody synth motif.
prompt.overview: References are most reliable when converted into H3 Context-IR. Only media in the Refs box receives attachment tags: picker images start at <Picture 1>. The first and last frames constrain the target timeline and are not numbered references. Define reusable identity/content as <Subject N>, cite its source tag, and describe its preservation in retention_analysis. Video soundtracks consume <Audio N> labels before standalone audio, so audio numbering can shift when a reference video contains sound.
prompt.instructions: Use all six headings in order. In subject_definitions, define each reusable person, object, scene, style, action, or voice as <Subject N> and cite the source attachment tag. In summary, identify the task as [reference generation] and assign each reference a role. In retention_analysis, mark important identities fully_preserved and list the exact traits that must remain. In detailed_description, describe each shot, action, composition, lighting, camera movement, dialogue, and when each subject appears. Finish with overall_soundscape and non_diegetic_music. Picture and video tags are 1-based per type. Audio tags are also 1-based, but a connected video soundtrack receives an audio label before standalone audio clips.
do: Use all six Context-IR sections in the documented order
Define <Subject N> from exact <Picture N>/<Video N>/<Audio N> sources
State identity-critical traits explicitly and mark them fully_preserved
Assign each reference one or more clear roles: identity, style, setting, motion, camera, or voice
Describe visible action, composition, lighting, and camera movement shot by shot
Describe ambience and effects in overall_soundscape and score in non_diegetic_music
Use <d>[Language] spoken words</d> for dialogue when exact speech matters
dont: Don't mention only <Picture 1> and assume H3 will infer which subject or traits must be retained
Don't use <Image N>/<Photo N>; attachment source tags are <Picture N>/<Video N>/<Audio N>
Don't label a standalone clip <Audio 1> without accounting for earlier reference-video soundtracks
Don't rely on negative prompts — this is a distilled model
Don't omit retention_analysis or the two audio sections
examples: subject_definitions: <Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>; preserve her facial identity, hair, age, and clothing. summary: [reference generation] <Subject 1> walks through a sunlit plaza. retention_analysis: <Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain all identity-defining traits from <Picture 1>. detailed_description: [Shot 1] <Subject 1> walks slowly toward the camera while a steady dolly-back keeps her centered. overall_soundscape: Soft crowd murmur and a distant fountain. non_diegetic_music: Gentle acoustic guitar.

subject_definitions: <Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>; her appearance is preserved, while her walking motion, setting, lighting, and camera path come from <Video 1>. summary: [reference generation] Transfer <Video 1>'s scene and motion to <Subject 1>. retention_analysis: <Subject 1>: fully_preserved - keep her identity and clothing; <Video 1>: attribute_transfer - reuse its motion, setting, lighting, and camera. detailed_description: Describe the transferred shot beat by beat. overall_soundscape: Reference the appropriate <Audio N> after accounting for the soundtrack paired with <Video 1>. non_diegetic_music: Preserve or describe the intended score.

speed.measured_note: large video model with a 32B text encoder; reference tokens ride every sampling step. Not yet benchmarked on this box.

ui_help.note: Generate a clip WITH sound from reference media. For reliable identity, define <Subject N> from each attachment and include retention_analysis plus the documented Context-IR sections.

edit_use_cases: reference-to-video: generate a clip featuring the referenced subject, with native audio

reference.hint: Only files in this Refs box are numbered: picker images are <Picture 1>…<Picture 9>. The first/last frames are timeline anchors, not references. Define reusable content as <Subject N> sourced from attachment tags. Video soundtracks take <Audio N> labels before standalone audio, and H3 allows at most 12 reference files total.
